questions.question: Which role grants access to create, manage, and add users to groups within Lifecycle Events?

explanation.correct: The Lifecycle Events administrator [sn_hr_le.admin] role grants access to create, manage, and add users to groups within Lifecycle Events. This role can access Guided Setup, Manage Owner Groups, Manage Roles, LE UI Configuration, and Executive Dashboards. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_hr_le.activity_reader can only read HR activity sets and activities, not manage them.
sn_hr_le.case_writer can create Lifecycle Events cases but not manage groups or users.
sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager can activate and trigger activity sets but not manage users.

source.excerpt: Lifecycle Events administrator [sn_hr_le.admin] - Grants access to create, manage, and add users to groups within Lifecycle Events. Can access: Guided Setup, Manage Owner Groups, Manage Roles, LE UI Configuration, Onboarding Executive Dashboard.

questions.question: What is the plugin name for Lifecycle Events in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: The Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events plugin has the name [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events]. This plugin installs several types of components including tables and user roles. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: com.sn_hr_core is the core HR plugin, not specifically for Lifecycle Events.
This is not a valid ServiceNow plugin name.
This is not a valid ServiceNow plugin name.

source.excerpt: Several types of components install with the activation of the Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] plugin, including tables and user roles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the sn_hr_le.min_admin_count system property?

options.text: Sets the minimum number of activities in a lifecycle event
Prevents deleting your only Enterprise Onboarding admin by requiring a minimum number of active users with the role
Limits the number of concurrent lifecycle events
Sets the minimum approval count for HR cases

explanation.correct: The sn_hr_le.min_admin_count system property helps prevent you from deleting your only Enterprise Onboarding and Transition admin user by requiring a minimum number (the default is two) of active users with this role. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property controls admin user count, not activity count.
Concurrent lifecycle events are not controlled by this property.
HR case approvals are not related to this admin count property.

source.excerpt: The Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] plugin activates the sn_hr_le.min_admin_count system property. This property helps to prevent you from deleting your only Enterprise Onboarding and Transition admin user by requiring a minimum number (the default is two) of active users with this role.

questions.question: Which tables are installed with the Lifecycle Events plugin? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: The Lifecycle Events plugin installs several tables including: Activity [sn_hr_le_activity] for activity details, Activity Set [sn_hr_le_activity set] for activity set details, and HR Lifecycle Events Case [sn_hr_le_case] for submitted lifecycle event case details. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_hr_le_schedule is not a table installed with Lifecycle Events.
sn_hr_le_journey is not a table installed with Lifecycle Events.

source.excerpt: Activity [sn_hr_le_activity] - Details of activities that are part of an activity set. Activity Set [sn_hr_le_activity set] - Details of activity sets and activities that make up Lifecycle Events. HR Lifecycle Events Case [sn_hr_le_case] - Details of a submitted Lifecycle Events case.

questions.question: What does the Activity Set Context table track in Lifecycle Events?

options.text: The employee information for each activity
The state of each Activity Set when the lifecycle event initializes (triggered, waiting for activities, etc.)
The approval history for activity sets
The cost center assignment for activities

explanation.correct: The Activity Set Context [sn_hr_le_activity_set_context] table is created for each Activity Set when the lifecycle event initializes. It tracks the state of each set (triggered, waiting for activities to complete, and more). It works with the Activity Status table to provide filtering for the Lifecycle Events widget. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Employee information is tracked in the HR Profile and Case tables, not Activity Set Context.
Approval history is tracked in approval-specific tables, not Activity Set Context.
Cost center assignments are not tracked in Activity Set Context.

source.excerpt: Activity Set Context [sn_hr_le_activity_set_context] - Created for each Activity Set when the life cycle event initializes. Tracks the state of each set (triggered, waiting for activities to complete, and more). Works with the Activity Status table to provide filtering for the Lifecycle Events widget.

questions.question: Which role can activate and trigger HR activity sets?

explanation.correct: The Activity set manager [sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager] role can activate and trigger HR activity sets. This role contains the sn_hr_le.activity_writer role which allows creating activity sets and activities. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_hr_le.activity_reader can only read activity sets and activities, not activate them.
sn_hr_le.activity_writer can create activity sets but cannot activate or trigger them.
sn_hr_le.case_reader can read Lifecycle Events cases but not manage activity sets.

source.excerpt: Activity set manager [sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager] - Can activate and trigger HR activity sets. Contains roles: sn_hr_le.activity_writer

questions.question: Which is NOT a supported family release for Journey Accelerator Version 4.0.2?

explanation.correct: Rome is NOT a supported release for Journey Accelerator Version 4.0.2. The supported family releases are Utah, Tokyo, and San Diego. Rome is supported in earlier versions like 3.0.3, 2.0.2, and 2.0.1. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/journey-accelerator/ja-version-support.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Utah is explicitly listed as a supported release for version 4.0.2.
Tokyo is explicitly listed as a supported release for version 4.0.2.
San Diego is explicitly listed as a supported release for version 4.0.2.

source.excerpt: Journey Accelerator Version 4.0.2 - Supported family releases: Utah, Tokyo, San Diego.

questions.question: Which spoke must be installed to schedule Outlook meetings from Journey Accelerator task-based to-dos?

explanation.correct: To schedule Outlook meetings from Journey Accelerator task-based to-dos, the Microsoft Exchange Online Spoke [sn_ex_online_spke] and Retry Handler Framework should be installed. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/journey-accelerator/ja-version-support.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Microsoft AD Spoke is for Active Directory integration, not Outlook scheduling.
Microsoft Azure AD Spoke is for Azure Active Directory, not Outlook meetings.
Microsoft Teams Spoke is for Teams integration, not Outlook meeting scheduling.

source.excerpt: To schedule Outlook meetings from Journey Accelerator tasked-based to-dos, the following spoke should be installed: Microsoft Exchange Online Spoke v3.2.0 [sn_ex_online_spke]

questions.question: What is significant about Journey Accelerator Version 5.0.0?

options.text: It is the first version to support mobile devices
It cannot be installed as a standalone application and is installed as a dependency with Journey Designer
It requires a separate license from ServiceNow
It only supports the Xanadu release

explanation.correct: Journey Accelerator Version 5.0.0 cannot be installed as a standalone application. Journey Accelerator version 5 functionality is installed as a dependency with Journey Designer version 1. This represents a major architectural change in how Journey Accelerator is deployed. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/journey-accelerator/ja-version-support.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Mobile support is not specifically called out as a change in version 5.0.0.
Licensing requirements are not mentioned as a change for version 5.0.0.
Version 5.0.4 is supported on Tokyo release, not only Xanadu.

source.excerpt: Journey Accelerator Version 5.0.0 cannot be installed as a standalone application. Journey Accelerator version 5 functionality is installed as a dependency with Journey designer version 1.

questions.question: Which update sets must be loaded after installing Journey Accelerator? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: After installing Journey Accelerator, the following update sets must be loaded: JA_ESC_header_menu_item-Journey Accelerator_Plans.xml, JA_Enforce_security_property.xml, and JA_Allow_Content_Delivery.xml. These are linked in the Supporting Links and Documentation section of the ServiceNow Store. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/journey-accelerator/ja-version-support.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: JA_Enable_mobile_access.xml is not a required update set for Journey Accelerator.
JA_Database_upgrade.xml is not a required update set for Journey Accelerator.

source.excerpt: The following update sets must be loaded after installing Journey Accelerator: JA_ESC_header_menu_item-Journey Accelerator_Plans.xml, JA_Enforce_security_property.xml, JA_Allow_Content_Delivery.xml

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Activity Field Mapping table in Lifecycle Events?

options.text: Passes information from the parent lifecycle event case to an activity
Maps field names between ServiceNow and external systems
Defines field validation rules for activities

explanation.correct: The Activity Field Mapping [sn_hr_le_activity_field_mapping] table stores details of activity field mappings that pass information from the parent lifecycle event case to an activity. This enables data to flow from the case to individual activities. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Employee profile mapping is handled through HR Profile tables, not Activity Field Mapping.
External system integration field mapping is handled by import sets, not this table.
Field validation rules are configured separately, not in Activity Field Mapping.

source.excerpt: Activity Field Mapping [sn_hr_le_activity_field_mapping] - Details of an activity field mapping that pass information from the parent life cycle event case to an activity.

questions.question: After the Lifecycle Events plugin is installed, the sn_hr_le.admin role is automatically assigned to which role?

explanation.correct: After the Lifecycle Events plugin is installed, the Lifecycle Events administrator (sn_hr_le.admin) role is automatically assigned to the IT system administrator (admin) role. Administrators should then assign sn_hr_le.admin to at least two users and remove it from the admin role to suppress IT administrators from viewing sensitive HR information. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_hr_core.manager doesn't automatically receive the LE admin role.
The itil role doesn't automatically receive the LE admin role.
hr_manager is not a standard ServiceNow role; the LE admin goes to the admin role.

source.excerpt: After the Lifecycle Events plugin is installed, the Lifecycle Events administrator (sn_hr_le.admin) role is automatically assigned to the IT system administrator (admin) role. Use the admin role to assign the sn_hr_le.admin role to at least two users in your organization.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true about Lifecycle Events roles?
a) The sn_hr_le.case_writer role contains sn_hr_core.case_writer
b) The sn_hr_le.activity_reader role contains no other roles
c) The sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager role contains sn_hr_le.activity_writer
d) The sn_hr_le.admin role contains skill_admin

options.text: Only a and b are true
Only b, c, and d are true
All statements (a, b, c, d) are true
Only c and d are true

explanation.correct: All four statements are true. The sn_hr_le.case_writer contains sn_hr_core.case_writer. The sn_hr_le.activity_reader contains no other roles. The sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager contains sn_hr_le.activity_writer. The sn_hr_le.admin contains skill_admin along with several other roles. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statements c and d are also true, not just a and b.
Statement a is also true, making all four statements correct.
Statements a and b are also true.

source.excerpt: Case writer [sn_hr_le.case_writer] - Contains roles: sn_hr_core.case_writer. Activity reader [sn_hr_le.activity_reader] - Contains roles: None. Activity set manager [sn_hr_le.activity_set_manager] - Contains roles: sn_hr_le.activity_writer. Lifecycle Events administrator [sn_hr_le.admin] - Contains roles: skill_admin...

questions.question: What is the purpose of Lifecycle Events Types?

options.text: Organize activity sets and activities together as a container, associated with an HR Service

explanation.correct: Lifecycle Events Types [sn_hr_le_type] are a way to organize activity sets and activities together. Lifecycle Events Types act as a container for activity sets and activities. They are also associated with an HR Service. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Employee categories are defined through HR Criteria, not Lifecycle Events Types.
Case priority is a separate field on HR cases, not related to LE Types.
Approval types are configured in workflow or approval rules, not LE Types.

source.excerpt: Lifecycle Events Type [sn_hr_le_type] - Lifecycle Events Types are a way to organize activity sets and activities together. Lifecycle Events Types act as a container for activity sets and activities. Lifecycle Events Types are also associated with an HR Service.

questions.question: Which table tracks details about activities waiting to be triggered in Lifecycle Events?

explanation.correct: The Future To-dos [sn_hr_le_future_todo] table tracks details about activities waiting to be triggered. This table holds pending activities that have not yet met their trigger conditions. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Activity Status tracks the state of activities already triggered, not pending ones.
Activity Set Context tracks the state of activity sets, not individual future activities.
Activity Base is the base table for activities but doesn't specifically track future/pending activities.

source.excerpt: Future To-dos [sn_hr_le_future_todo] - Tracks details about activities waiting to be triggered.

questions.question: An organization is implementing Lifecycle Events and wants the administrator role to also be able to configure COEs. Which additional role must be combined with sn_hr_le.admin?

explanation.correct: The Lifecycle Events administrator (sn_hr_le.admin) role with the Delegated Developer (delegated_developer) role can also configure and create COEs (Centers of Excellence). This combination enables HR administrators to manage both Lifecycle Events and COE configuration. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/employee-service-management/lifecycle-events/components-installed-with-enterprise-onboarding-and-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_hr_core.manager provides case and profile access but not COE configuration capabilities.
sn_hr_core.case_writer is for creating cases, not configuring COEs.
skill_admin is already contained in sn_hr_le.admin and is not specifically for COE configuration.

source.excerpt: The Lifecycle Events administrator (sn_hr_le.admin) role with the Delegated Developer (delegated_developer) role can also configure and create COEs.
